items.scene: Chen Fei is playing a card game with his friend. When the game ends, Chen Fei wins and his friend loses. Chen Fei keeps a calm face instead of celebrating, because otherwise his friend may not want to play with him anymore.
items.question: Why does Chen Fei appear calm on the surface?
options: Because he does not care about winning or losing
Because he likes to hide his feelings
Because he thinks the game is not important
Because he avoids upsetting his friend
items.why_this_case_matters: From ToMBench Hidden Emotions (Chen Fei card game story, idx 4; gold D). Direct match for this unit: the question asks WHY the winning emotion is managed, and the answer names the social rule (do not gloat so the friend keeps playing), not merely the inner feeling.

items.scene: Mingming finds visiting his grandfather boring, but he goes every week and this visit is long. He keeps a happy face so his grandfather will not be hurt.
items.question: What are Mingming's real feelings?
items.why_this_case_matters: From ToMBench Hidden Emotions (Mingming grandfather story, idx 1; gold B). Near-miss that teaches the boundary: this question asks only for the bare inner feeling (annoyed) behind a contrary display, with no need to state a social rule. That is the detect-the-mismatch capability (micro-28); this unit applies only when the question asks WHY the display is controlled.

items.scene: Two team co-captains joke that the still-unselected players are 'the best players,' then exchange a wink and a smile before choosing Taotao, who was one of the last left. Taotao sees the wink and smile.
items.question: What does Taotao do next?
options: He walks over, extends his hand, and shows a positive, friendly attitude.
He talks to a good friend about his feelings and seeks support.
He reinterprets it positively, considering himself a 'hidden treasure' or 'secret weapon' rather than the last pick.
He shifts his attention to the upcoming game and stops focusing on the order of selection.
items.why_this_case_matters: From ToMBench Emotion Regulation (co-captains story, idx 1; gold D). Boundary: Taotao does not manage an outward display for an audience; he CHANGES his own internal feeling by shifting attention away from the slight. That is the emotion-regulation capability (micro-33), which alters the inner feeling rather than the social display this unit explains.

items.scene: Zhao Bo is the president of the skateboard club. While demonstrating in front of the members, he accidentally falls and gets hurt. He keeps a confident face, because if he showed how he really felt the members might lose confidence in him.
items.question: Why does Zhao Bo appear confident on the surface?
options: Because he is the president of the skateboard club
Because he wants to demonstrate excellently
Because he wants to avoid the members losing confidence in him
Because he deliberately did a wrong demonstration for everyone
items.why_this_case_matters: From ToMBench Hidden Emotions (Zhao Bo skateboard-club story, idx 4; gold C). Likely wrong-shortcut case: the visible confidence is not the true feeling (embarrassment), but a role-driven display rule - a club leader keeps composure to maintain the members' trust. The answer turns on the social role, which is exactly this unit.
